subject: EVS
chapter: Chapter 8: Clothes — How Things are Made
central_question: How do fibres become thread and fabric through spinning, weaving and stitching, and how do Indian traditions encourage skill, creativity and reuse?
in_scope_units: Patterns with Threads: natural artists, the baya weaver and the meaning of weaving.
Activities 1–2: paper-strip weaving and observing the criss-cross pattern in cloth.
Traditions of Weaving: loom, handloom fabric, regional traditions, livelihood and textile mills.
Thread and Activity 3: pulling and twisting cotton, spinning, yarn, fibre, charkha and khadi.
Natural and synthetic fibres: bamboo, cotton, linen, wool, silk, nylon, rayon, polyester and terylene.
Silk and the silkworm life cycle: eggs, caterpillar, cocoon and moth.
Activity 4: identifying natural and synthetic materials in everyday items.
Crafting with Needle and Thread: tailorbird, leaf construction and Activity 5.
Activities 6–8: finding stitches, learning running stitch and joining cloth pieces.
Stitch and Decorate: traditional embroideries and their regional origins.
Recycle and Exhibition: passing on clothes, repurposing scraps, quilts and displaying student work.
Let us reflect, Questions 1–7: reuse, importance of threads, local traditions, moth life cycle and cloth observation.
banned_topics: General energy sources and electricity safety from Chapter 7.
Day–night and seasonal rhythms from Chapter 9.
Worldwide movement of foods, animals and ideas from Chapter 10.

known_pitfalls.claim: Weaving means tying a single thread into knots.
known_pitfalls.correction: Weaving crosses one set of strips or threads with another in an over-and-under pattern.

known_pitfalls.claim: Spinning and weaving are the same process.
known_pitfalls.correction: Spinning twists fibres into yarn; weaving crosses threads to form fabric.

known_pitfalls.claim: All fibres come from plants or animals.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter also includes synthetic fibres made by humans.

known_pitfalls.claim: Needles may be used freely after the stitching lesson.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter requires careful handling and close adult supervision.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Activity 1: demonstrate the over–under structure of weaving.
NCERT Activity 2: identify the criss-cross pattern in cloth.
NCERT Activity 3: distinguish fibre, spinning and yarn.
NCERT Activity 4: classify everyday items as natural or synthetic.
NCERT Activity 7: explain the sequence of a running stitch.
NCERT Activity 8: join scraps to create a useful object.
NCERT Let us reflect, Question 6: order the silk moth life cycle.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter section is ‘Let us reflect’, Questions 1–7 on pages 143–144.
